about.title: Upland Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Upland sits where the 210 meets the foothills, and the daily rhythm of the city shows up in its collision records. In 2025, the most recent final reporting year, Upland logged 430 injury collisions, with 628 people hurt and 2 lives lost. Public-record counts run highest along SR-210, Euclid Avenue, Mountain Avenue, and Foothill Boulevard, and reports cluster on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters and weekend traffic overlap. If you were one of those 628 people, the days after a crash can feel like paperwork piled on top of pain. LawProactive exists to take one task off that pile. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that matches you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles San Bernardino County car accident claims on a contingency basis. That attorney can help you gather photos, witness names, and medical records before they fade, and can deal with the other driver's insurer so you do not have to.

items.title: You Keep Every Dollar You Recover Until the End
items.desc: Attorneys in our network take car accident cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case results in a recovery. Our matching service costs you nothing at any stage.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not Close the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still pursue a claim even if you shared some blame for a crash on Mountain Avenue or Foothill Boulevard. Your recovery is simply reduced by your share of responsibility.

items.title: Deadlines Get Tracked From Day One
items.desc: Most California car accident claims must be filed within two years, but a claim against a city, county, or state agency can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney can pin down which clock applies to your situation before it runs.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement about my crash on the 210 in Upland. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are generally not obligated to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and doing so before speaking with an attorney can work against you. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that shrink claims. It is reasonable to decline politely and let an attorney handle communication with the insurer on your behalf.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering after a California car accident?
items.answer: California does not cap non-economic damages in ordinary car accident cases, so compensation for pain, emotional distress, and loss of enjoyment of life is decided on the facts rather than a fixed ceiling. Economic losses like medical bills and missed wages are calculated separately. An attorney can explain how both categories apply to your injuries.

items.question: What should I save after a crash if I want to protect my claim?
items.answer: Photos of the vehicles, the road, and your injuries matter a great deal, as do the names and numbers of anyone who saw what happened. Keep every medical record, receipt, and piece of correspondence from insurers, and ask for a copy of the police report. Evidence like nearby camera footage can disappear quickly, so getting an attorney involved early helps preserve it.
